findings.evidence: Lines 45–49 take `hInvDiff : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun t => (A t).inverse) 0` and immediately obtain `hInvRaw := hInvDiff.hasDerivAt`; lines 75–80 and ParametricPullback.lean:47,58 merely pass this assumption onward.
findings.fix: Prove differentiability of `t ↦ (A t).inverse` from differentiability at the identity, adding an appropriate completeness assumption on `E` if required by the inverse-map theorem, then remove `hInvDiff` from all three declarations.
findings.issue: `HasDerivAt.clm_inverse_apply` assumes `hInvDiff`, which already contains the difficult existence of the derivative of the inverse family; the proof only identifies that assumed derivative. The same assumption propagates into `clm_inverse_apply_comp` (line 75) and `hasDerivAt_pullback_parametric` (ParametricPullback.lean:47), leaving the claimed pullback theorem unavailable from ordinary smooth-family/invertibility data.

summary: The central differentiability of the inverse Jacobian is assumed rather than established, so the PR does not supply its advertised analytic prerequisite.
